answer: In an agent-run insurance pool for a tundra town's coastal garden, members vote on damage claims after each tide. Voting weight comes from collateral locked for a full season, and each unit of collateral can back only one vote. Splitting funds among ten aliases creates no extra weight; to sway a claim an attacker must lock more capital and risk losing it if fabricated evidence is challenged. A wealthy coalition can still dominate, while small honest members may lack stake, so cap large positions and have randomly selected auditors check sensor records before payment.
